questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience life in another european city as well as wanting to feel close to home in order to have friends and family visit during my stay. As I am also a student studying with a chronic illness it was important to me that I knew the country I would study in had somewhat a similar lifestyle allowing me to stay in my routine that helps me navigate my illness. It was furthermore crucial to me to choose a university with high ranking of academic skills as well as choosing a city and country allowing me to experience different aspects of the culture within the country. I was i Zürich and really appreciated being able to experience Switzerland's mountains.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dorm that was offered to us as exchange students was not the best and affected my social experience. Furthermore the kitchen was extremely difficult and in bad condition making it close to impossible to actually cook food and I ended up spending double my budget on food.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: . I found that the office for incoming students at UZH was extremely helpful and prepared me well, sending relevant documents and links in time letting me know how I should manage. I was surprised by the extra administrative work when arriving in Switzerland, with having to register at the Kreisbüro/Stadthouse, health insurance and rental agreement, as I was not prepared for it to be part of the administrative preparation and how much time and effort that had to be put into it and also the cost of it, came as a bit of a surprise for me, but the office for incoming students at UZH was extremely helpful with the guides they sent out with mail, and furthermore living with other exchange students to ask for advice. The preparation was a bit of a hazzle and cause of frustration due to separate deadlines and processing time at my home university that didn’t match up with UZH, but the student counselling was very helpful at both universities to make it work, and it worked out in the end. Furthermore, I am an exchange student studying with disabilities, studying part time with exemption due to chronic illness. This of course gave me some more preparation due to having to receive exemption from both my home university and host university, but I found that it was absolutely no problem with UZH. It can be a bit overwhelming with all the administrative work, so I would recommend keeping it organized, seeking help, asking friends and start early.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found that the instructors at UZH were really engaged, dedicated and ambitious with their academic research and my classes were very inspiring and has been very profound for furthering my academic competences. I have enjoyed and appreciated the study environment and academic level of UZH. Something I very much appreciated was the teaching style as well, encouraging students to be active learners, participating in discussion, giving suggestions for the reading lists, and also the instructors inviting different speakers to be the expert on research themes, arranging excursions within Zürich (this was a great bonus as an exchange student to further understand the culture of Switzerland) and also bringing in relevant, interesting and current casework. UZH is also very well prepared and a great environment for exchange students providing an international community, making it approachable to study as a non-Swiss student. And the Incoming office guides you all the way and have already prepared answers to all your questions, not one time did I feel like I didn't know what to do or how to handle as they had already prepared me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I attended the mandatory introduction at Zürich University but really missed a more comprehensive introductory week of activities to meet other exchange students in an environment focusing on social relations.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I signed up for a dorm room through my host institution. The housing market in Zürich is really expensive and really difficult to find anything available - even more difficult than Copenhagen. So I was extremely happy to receive a room at the dorm and not having to find a housing option by self. 

I am extremely happy that I chose to stay in a dorm for exchange students offered through the mobility program. Doing so made the process of finding accommodation much easier and felt safer, as there are a lot of stories of exchange students being scammed, not being able to know what housing you get into and knowing you had a stable place to stay during the whole time of your exchange. Everything with WOKO was extremely well structured and clear on the instructions. It has been nice to stay at a place with other exchange students to quickly get a social network and being able to help each other with settling in and not feeling alone. The process was different than expected, as I was under the impression that you would be able to state wishes for the accommodation and I had read about the different dorms WOKO has to offer, and when being offered the room, you were offered just one room and had to accept it extremely quickly within 48 hours.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will live a bit outside of the city or city center, which will maybe increase your budget for transport. You options for grocery shopping may also be a bit limited. Otherwise I found it to be no problem at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I would have wished there had been more focus on social events for exchange students to get to know each other, that was not necessarily something that had to be arranged by ourselves. I found that especially at my dorm with 170 people, there quickly became groups that were exclusive of other students, as well as the groups being defined by the same nationality. I had hoped to have had a more social experience with mixed cultures but found that the large group I could more easily participate in was the one of my own nationalities, which was not a wish of mine. I found friendships outside of my dorm.

I found the WOKO dorm at Meierwiesenstrasse to be a bit of a challenge sometimes to stay in, as the kitchen is extremely small for 170 people to share all together and in extremely bad condition, it has led me to not want to cook very often and having to spend a lot of money on either prepared/ takeout food or eating very poorly and sometimes skipping meals. The pans in the kitchen are in such bad condition that you would become sick by using them. Furthermore, there were housing rules regarding noise which very often were not met, and I had a lot of trouble sleeping/ studying for the first few months until it dialed down due to exams and the weather, especially studying with a disability this was quite overwhelming and caused me some issues and I had hoped to stay at a smaller dorm than one for 170 people. There were issues with receiving the keys as well at the beginning of our stay. With that being said, I very much appreciated the private rooms and the great conditions of the property in general and the daily cleaning as well as appreciation for not having to search for my own accommodation. The location of the dorm was also extremely convenient, and it was super nice to have a nice room, with private sink, dishes and furniture included.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The process of booking courses was a bit different, than what I am used to. You have to make sure yourself that every course go together and dont intersect. I struggled a bit with having to organize my own classes across day/time/location and found it to be a bit of an issue, also when I had chosen different classes that fit with time/day/location, that some of them still would intercross on certain times with exams. But the teachers were very helpful and solutions oriented in making it work. Furthermore you could sign up for the courses and try them out and then cancel them by October, making it possible to try out which ones you prefer. I did not take part in that option as I needed the pre-approval of courses beforehand. 

Some of the courses had limited participants to it was a good option to book more courses than needed to be sure to get a spot and then cancel afterwards. 

Also you needed to be aware if the course was at the level for your studies as well as taught in english.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or email the incoming student office and they answered within very short time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the courses I had hoped

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Try to find courses in academic fields you know before hand, this gives an advantage when studying at a different university as you already have so beforehand knowledge and therefore can more quickly understand the theme presented from a different point of view. Also be aware your course is taught in english if thats important to you, this also gives you the opportunity to engage with other exchange students. 

And something I found I had been really smart about was to choose courses with exams that you feel confident in as well as exams that was done before Christmas. Being strategic about this allowed me to nit be stressed about exams, receiving good grades as well as being able to enjoy the end of my semester without exams to focus on traveling to places I had missed as well as saying goodbye to friends I made and organize my moving-out/de-register/arriving home process in a much more relaxed way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am really going to miss studying at UZH, it has been an absolute pleasure and privilege to attend a semester of my master’s at the University of Zürich. I found that both the instructors and the students were really engaged, dedicated and ambitious with their academic research and my classes were very inspiring and has been very profound for furthering my academic competences. I have enjoyed and appreciated the study environment and academic level of UZH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Something I very much appreciated was the teaching style as well, encouraging students to be active learners, participating in discussion, giving suggestions for the reading lists, and also the instructors inviting different speakers to be the expert on research themes, arranging excursions within Zürich (this was a great bonus as an exchange student to further understand the culture of Switzerland) and also bringing in relevant, interesting and current casework.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to postcolonial studies
Rethinking sexualities, intimacies and normativities
Gender, work and space

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of my courses: Introduction to postcolonial studies, Rethinking sexualities, intimacies and normativities and Gender, work and space. I think all of the courses were interesting and relevant and presented me with the newest research, all of the teachers were extremely dedicated and extremely good teachers. Each course gave me something different and each course was of my personal academic interest and furthered my academic skills. The courses also enlightened me on some of the same themes but from different perspectives.

questions.answer: For registering and de-registering living in Zürich I had to pay each time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation and food options in Switzerland were much more expensive that participated, as well as having to spend more money on food due to the kitchen facilities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Free sports facilities at university
Free cultural walk in the city at the beginning of the semester
One introduction at uni

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To participate in introductions as its where you will get relevant information and meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the swiss mountains - they are magnificent and extraordinary and is such a wonderful way to spend your weekends and getting a study break.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was extremely easy as Switzerland is not that much different to Denmark and as I have travelled to similar countries before. Especially in Zürich there is also a great international environment making it really easy to adapt. I have found it easy to integrate into the local culture and navigate the life of being a student at UZH. It has given me a great personal understanding of what it takes to work internationally as well as establishing a new life and everyday habits in a different country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, say yes, ask, stay curious and dont be afraid to invite yourself. And its also okay to not want to socialize all the time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Switzerland is very conservative, there are a lot of strict rules and normative hierarchical behaviour that I had to get used to, but it was not at to any extent that I found challenged my stay. 

Everything was extremely expensive, and it also sometimes felt like they would make money wherever they could.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Following the conservative culture and strict rules also comes a very well organized society making different processes run smoothly and effectively and therefore easy to navigate in. For example their trains alway run one time :) I have felt extremely comfortable and safe in Zürich. 

And also coming from the expensive lifestyle is a high living standard which is really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Appreciate the high academic level of the teachers and choose courses you are knowledgable in beforehand.
- Apply for a lot of scholarships, Switzerland is expensive and even more expensive than you might realize.
- GO TO THE MOUNTAINS!!! They are breathtaking and the swiss nature is just amazing, check in for the season to make sure its open and not dangerous, its a great way also to socialize with new friends as you usually go in groups with other exchange students. And gives you so much more energy and motivation to do academic work in between. Sunday is the day everyone goes as the stores are closed.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Academically, UZH have provided an exceptional environment that have strengthened my academic competences and enriched my educational experience and challenged my perspective to research. The international community at UZH facilitated a smooth transition for exchange students and the office for incoming students have been of great guidance and help. I have been very pleasantly surprised, as it has been positively more ambitious than what I am used to. The University of Zürich and the education provided to me during my exchange semester, is one of the things I will miss the most. I feel extremely privileged to have been able to receive such high level of educational improvement.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Life in Switzerland has been an absolute pleasure, of traditional and modern cultural experiences, personal growth, and the joys of Zürich living standards. The city's cultural offerings and the opportunities for nature experiences, with hikes in the weekend has contributed significantly to my overall experience.

Ultimately, my time in Zürich has been marked by comfort, safety, and easy integration into local culture, led by the incoming team at UZH. The experience offered not just academic growth but also valuable insights into working internationally and establishing a life in a foreign country. Personally, it has made me a more solutions-oriented, culturally aware, and globally conscious individual and has provided me with a great personal experience that has contributed to my worth of self and a new perspective on the life I live and the culture I come from.

I am really going to miss studying at UZH, it has been an absolute pleasure and privilege to attend a semester of my master’s at the University of Zürich. I found that both the instructors and the students were really engaged, dedicated and ambitious with their academic research and my classes were very inspiring and has been very profound for furthering my academic competences. 

Overall, it has been an extremely enriching experience both personally and academically and I would recommend everyone who can to study at UZH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Something that has been a challenge has been to keep up with my physical health, especially when suffering from a chronic illness, I am forced to take great care of my health, but it has been difficult to eat as healthy as I usually do, due to the conditions of the kitchen. It has also been difficult to exercise, even though UZH offers free exercise at campus (which I think is great), I have usually found the classes to be an overwhelmingly large number of participants as well as the classes and the app descriptions to being only in Swiss and having to take public transport for at least 30-40 min to go. I have looked up the options to become a member at a fitness-center, but the expenses for that have been way above my budget. I have tried to exercise in my room and outside as much as possible, but it has felt isolated and not as giving as doing it in a proper space.  

I would have wished there had been more focus on social events for exchange students to get to know each other, that was not necessarily something that had to be arranged by ourselves. I found that especially at my dorm with 170 people with one kitchen was overwhelming and caused me to isolate in my room more than I had wished to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I chose my exchange to be close to my home country to have friends and family visit as well as going home for Christmas, an opportunity I have appreciated very much and have been a bonus to my exchange to be able to share it with people I care about from home.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
